231: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
232: //
233: // Unbounded Log
234: // =============
235: //
236: // The UnboundedLog is the first Refinement of the SimpleLog. As its name suggests, it also uses
237: // an unbounded log to represent updates to the data structure, however the log itself is represented
238: // by a map instead of a sequence. Moreover, the state machine also manages the data structure
239: // replicas.
240: //
241: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
242: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
243: // Read Only Operations
244: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
245: /// ReadonlyState: Tracking the progress of read-only queries
246: ///
247: /// Used to track the progress of a read-only queries on the data structure.
248: ///
249: /// A readonly query takes place on a given node (`nid`), and follows the following algorithm:
250: ///
251: ///  1. Read the global value 'version_upper_bound'.
252: ///  2. Wait until node-local value 'local_head' is greater than the value
253: ///     of 'version_upper_bound' that was read in step 1.
254: ///  3. Execute the query against the node-local replica and return the result.
255: ///
256: /// (In real life, the thread does not just sit around 'waiting' in step 2;
257: /// it might run a combiner phase in order to advance the local_head.)
258: ///
259: /// These 3 steps progress the status of the request through the cycle
260: ///    Init -> VersionUpperBound -> ReadyToRead -> Done
261: ///
262: /// Note that the request itself does not "care" which nodeId it takes place on;
263: /// we only track the nodeId to make sure that steps 2 and 3 use the same node.
264: ///
265: #[is_variant]
266: pub ghost enum ReadonlyState<DT: Dispatch> {
267:     /// a new read request that has come in
268:     Init { op: DT::ReadOperation },
269:     /// has read the version upper bound value
270:     VersionUpperBound { op: DT::ReadOperation, version_upper_bound: LogIdx },
271:     /// ready to read
272:     ReadyToRead { op: DT::ReadOperation, version_upper_bound: LogIdx, node_id: NodeId },
273:     /// read request is done
274:     Done { op: DT::ReadOperation, version_upper_bound: LogIdx, node_id: NodeId, ret: DT::Response },
275: }
276: 
277: impl<DT: Dispatch> ReadonlyState<DT> {
278:     pub open spec fn op(self) -> DT::ReadOperation {
279:         match self {
280:             ReadonlyState::Init { op, .. } => op,
281:             ReadonlyState::VersionUpperBound { op, .. } => op,
282:             ReadonlyState::ReadyToRead { op, .. } => op,
283:             ReadonlyState::Done { op, .. } => op,
284:         }
285:     }
286: }
287: 
288: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
289: // Update Operation
290: ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
291: ////////// Updates and the combiner phase
292: //
293: // This part is a lot more complex; the lifecycle of an "update" is inherently
294: // tied to the lifecycle of the combiner, so I have to explain the entire combiner
295: // cycle for this to make sense.
296: //
297: // In particular, the combiner cycle starts with some (potentially empty) bulk collection
298: // of Update requests, which all start in UpdateState::Init.
299: // By the end of the combiner cycle (when it has gone back to 'Ready'), all the updates
300: // in that collection will be in UpdateState::Done.
301: //
302: // The combiner works as follows (keep in mind this is abstracted a bit from the
303: // real implementation).
304: //
305: //  1. Advance the 'tail' value by 1 for each update in the collection.
306: //     This creates a "LogEntry" for the given op at the given index.
307: //     It also updates the update from UpdateState::Init to UpdateState::Placed.
308: //
309: //      Note: This always appends to the log; there are never any "holes" in the log,
310: //      and the 'tail' always marks the end of the log. The log is unbounded
311: //      and not garbage-collected.
312: //      Keep in mind that the 'log' here is just an abstraction, and the "cyclic buffer"
313: //      that physically stores the log entries in real life has additional complexities.
314: //      We do not handle those complexities at this level of abstraction.
315: //
316: //      Note: Even when we have a bulk collection of updates, we still append the log
317: //      entries one at a time, once for each update. This means the log entries might
318: //      interleave with those of another thread.
319: //      This is more permissive than the real implementation, which advances the
320: //      'tail' with a single CAS operation, meaning that all the log entries
321: //      for the cycle will be contiguous in the log.
322: //      In the original Linear Dafny NR project, we modeled this step as a bulk update,
323: //      matching the implemenation. However, it turned out that:
324: //          (i) modeling 'bulk update' steps is kind of annoying
325: //          (ii) we never took advantage of the contiguity in the invariants
326: //      Since the single-step version is easier to model, and we don't lose anything for it,
327: //      that's what we do here.
328: //
329: //  2. Read the 'local_head' value for the given node.
330: //
331: //  3. Read the global 'tail' value.
332: //
333: //  4. Process all log entries in the range local_head..tail.
334: //     (This should include both the log entries we just creates, plus maybe some other
335: //     log entries from other nodes.)
336: //
337: //      NOTE: the global 'tail' value might change over the course of execution,
338: //      but we're going to stick with the local copy that we just read
339: //      (i.e., the value on the stack).
340: //
341: //     To process a log entry, we first apply the operation to the replica, and get
342: //     back a "return value". Next, we check if the log entry is for the given nodeId,
343: //     classifying it as "remote" or "local".
344: //      - If it's remote, we're done.
345: //      - If it's local, then we find the Update object in our bulk collection, and
346: //        update it from UpdateState::Placed to UpdateState::Applied, recording the
347: //        return value.
348: //
349: //  5. Update the global value of 'version_upper_bound'.
350: //     This step lets us move all the updates to UpdateState::Done.
351: //
352: //  6. Update the value of 'local_head'.
353: //
354: // Now, there are a bunch of things we need to prove so that the whole thing makes sense
355: // and so that the implementation can actually follow along and return data to the clients.
356: //
357: // Specifically, we have a sequence of "return ids" (recorded in the 'queued_ops' field)
358: // that need to get processed. When the implementation handles a "local" operation off the
359: // log, it appends the return value into a buffer; when it's done, it expects the buffer
360: // of return values to line up with all the update requests that it started with.
361: //
362: // What this means is that we need to show:
363: //   - When we process a "local" operation, its ReqId corresponds to the next
364: //     ReqId recorded in the queued_ops (i.e., the one at 'queue_index'.)
365: //   - When we have finished the entire loop, we have finished processing all
366: //     the ReqIds we expected (i.e., `queue_index == queued_ops.len()`).
367: //
368: // This means we need to establish an invariant between the combiner state and the
369: // log state at all times. Specifically, we need an invariant that relates the combiner
370: // state to the log entries whose node_ids match the combiner's node, describing where
371: // they are and in what order.
372: //
373: // The invariant roughly says that during step (4), (the "Loop" state):
374: //   The ReqIds in `queued_ops`, sliced from queue_index .. queued_ops.len()
375: //   match
376: //   The ReqIds in the log that are local, sliced from
377: //          local_head .. tail
378: // (Note that queue_index and local_head are the cursors that advance throughout the loop,
379: // while tail is the one recorded in step 3, so it's fixed.)
380: // Furthermore:
381: //   There are no local operations in the log between
382: //   the recorded tail and the global tail.
383: // See the invariant `wf_combiner_for_node_id`, as well as the predicates
384: // `LogRangeMatchesQueue` and `LogRangeNoNodeId`.
385: //
386: // Example: suppose N is the local node_id, and [a, b, c, d] are the request ids.
387: // We might be in a state that looks like this: (Here, '...' indicates remote entries,
388: // and '(N, x)' means a log entry with node id N that corresponds to request id x.)
389: //
390: //       CombinerState                                           CombinerState   global
391: //       local_head                                              tail     tail
392: //          |                                                              |               |
393: //       ===================================================================================
394: //          |          |       |       |        |       |          |       |       |       |
395: //  Log:    |  (N, b)  |  ...  |  ...  | (N, c) |  ...  |  (N, d)  |  ...  |  ...  |  ...  |
396: //          |          |       |       |        |       |          |       |       |       |
397: //       ===================================================================================
398: //
399: //  ---- Combiner state (in `CombinerState::Loop` phase).
400: //
401: //      queued_ops =  [  a,   b,   c,   d   ]
402: //                          ^
403: //                          |
404: //                  queue_index = 1
405: //
406: // ---- Update state:
407: //
408: //    a => UpdateState::Applied { ... }
409: //    b => UpdateState::Placed { ... }
410: //    c => UpdateState::Placed { ... }
411: //    d => UpdateState::Placed { ... }
412: //
413: // In the example, `LogRangeMatchesQueue` is the relation that shows that (b, c, d)
414: // agree between the queued_ops and the log; whereas `LogRangeNoNodeId` shows that there
415: // are no more local entries between the Combiner tail and the global tail.
416: //
417: // And again, in the real implementation, b, c, d will actually be contiguous in the log,
418: // but the state shown above is permitted by the model here.
419: // If we _were_ going to make use of contiguity, then the place to do it would probably
420: // be the definition of `LogRangeMatchesQueue`, but as I explained earlier, I didn't
421: // find it helpful.
422: //
423: // Another technical note: the LogEntry doesn't actually store the ReqId on it;
424: // `LogRangeMatchesQueue` has to connect the request id to the UpdateState, which then
425: // has a pointer into the log via `idx`. (It's possible that this could be simplified.)
426: #[is_variant]
427: pub ghost enum UpdateState<DT: Dispatch> {
428:     /// upated request has entered the system
429:     Init { op: DT::WriteOperation },
430:     /// update has been placed into the log
431:     Placed { op: DT::WriteOperation, idx: LogIdx },
432:     /// the update has been applied to the data structure
433:     Applied { ret: DT::Response, idx: LogIdx },
434:     /// the update is ready to be returned
435:     Done { ret: DT::Response, idx: LogIdx },
436: }
437: 
438: #[is_variant]
439: pub ghost enum CombinerState {
440:     Ready,
441:     Placed { queued_ops: Seq<ReqId> },
442:     LoadedLocalVersion { queued_ops: Seq<ReqId>, lversion: LogIdx },
443:     Loop {
444:         /// sequence of request ids of the local node
445:         queued_ops: Seq<ReqId>,
446:         /// version of the local replica
447:         lversion: LogIdx,
448:         /// index into the queued ops
449:         idx: nat,
450:         /// the global tail we'v read
451:         tail: LogIdx,
452:     },
453:     UpdatedVersion { queued_ops: Seq<ReqId>, tail: LogIdx },
454: }
455: 
456: impl CombinerState {
457:     pub open spec fn queued_ops(self) -> Seq<ReqId> {
458:         match self {
459:             CombinerState::Ready => Seq::empty(),
460:             CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops } => queued_ops,
461:             CombinerState::LoadedLocalVersion { queued_ops, .. } => queued_ops,
462:             CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, .. } => queued_ops,
463:             CombinerState::UpdatedVersion { queued_ops, .. } => queued_ops,
464:         }
465:     }
466: 
467:     pub open spec fn queued_ops_set(&self) -> Set<ReqId> {
468:         seq_to_set(self.queued_ops())
469:     }
470: }
471: 
472: } // verus!

588:     #[invariant]
589:     pub fn inv_readonly_requests_wf(&self) -> bool {
590:         forall |rid| (#[trigger] self.local_reads.contains_key(rid))
591:              ==> self.wf_readstate(self.local_reads[rid])
592:     }
593: 
594:     pub open spec fn wf_readstate(&self, rs: ReadonlyState<DT>) -> bool {
595:         match rs {
596:             ReadonlyState::Init{op} => {
597:                 true
598:             }
599:             ReadonlyState::VersionUpperBound{op, version_upper_bound} => {
600:                 version_upper_bound <= self.version_upper_bound
601:             }
602:             ReadonlyState::ReadyToRead{op, node_id, version_upper_bound} => {
603:                 &&& self.wf_node_id(node_id)
604:                 &&& version_upper_bound <= self.version_upper_bound
605:                 &&& version_upper_bound <= self.current_local_version(node_id)
606:             }
607:             ReadonlyState::Done{op, ret, node_id, version_upper_bound } => {
608:                 &&& self.wf_node_id(node_id)
609:                 &&& version_upper_bound <= self.version_upper_bound
610:                 &&& version_upper_bound <= self.current_local_version(node_id)
611:             }
612:         }
613:     }

616:     /// the combiner states are wellformed
617:     /// Inv_CombinerStateValid(s)
618:     #[invariant]
619:     pub open spec fn combiner_states_wf(&self) -> bool {
620:         forall |node_id| (#[trigger] self.combiner.contains_key(node_id))
621:              ==> self.wf_combiner_for_node_id(node_id)
622:     }
623: 
624:     pub open spec fn wf_combiner_for_node_id(&self, node_id: NodeId) -> bool
625:         recommends self.wf_node_id(node_id)
626:     {
627:         match self.combiner[node_id] {
628:             CombinerState::Ready => {
629:                 // from other inv
630:                 // &&& self.local_versions.contains_key(node_id)
631:                 // &&& self.local_versions[node_id] <= self.tail
632:                 &&& LogRangeNoNodeId(self.log, self.local_versions[node_id], self.tail, node_id)
633:             }
634:             CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops } => {
635:                 // &&& self.local_versions.contains_key(node_id)
636:                 // &&& self.local_versions[node_id] <= self.tail
637:                 &&& LogRangeMatchesQueue(queued_ops, self.log, 0, self.local_versions[node_id], self.tail, node_id, self.local_updates)
638:                 &&& QueueRidsUpdatePlaced(queued_ops, self.local_updates, 0)
639:                 &&& seq_unique(queued_ops)
640:             }
641:             CombinerState::LoadedLocalVersion{ queued_ops, lversion } => {
642:                // we've just read the local tail value, and no-one else should modify that
643:                 &&& lversion == self.local_versions[node_id]
644:                 // by transitivity we have lversion <= self.version_upper_bound and self.tail
645:                 // the local tail should be smaller or equal than the ctail
646:                 // &&& lversion <= self.version_upper_bound
647:                 // &&& lversion <= self.tail
648:                 &&& LogRangeMatchesQueue(queued_ops, self.log, 0, lversion, self.tail, node_id, self.local_updates)
649:                 &&& QueueRidsUpdatePlaced(queued_ops, self.local_updates, 0)
650:                 &&& seq_unique(queued_ops)
651:             }
652:             CombinerState::Loop{ queued_ops, idx, lversion, tail } => {
653:                 // the global tail may have already advanced...
654:                 &&& tail <= self.tail
655:                 // we're advancing the local tail here
656:                 &&& lversion >= self.local_versions[node_id]
657:                 // the local tail should always be smaller or equal to the global tail
658:                 &&& lversion <= tail
659:                 // the log now contains all entries up to localtail
660:                 &&& LogContainsEntriesUpToHere(self.log, lversion)
661:                 &&& 0 <= idx <= queued_ops.len()
662:                 &&& LogRangeMatchesQueue(queued_ops, self.log, idx, lversion, tail, node_id, self.local_updates)
663:                 &&& LogRangeNoNodeId(self.log, tail, self.tail, node_id)
664:                 &&& QueueRidsUpdatePlaced(queued_ops, self.local_updates, idx)
665:                 &&& QueueRidsUpdateDone(queued_ops, self.local_updates, idx)
666:                 &&& seq_unique(queued_ops)
667:             }
668:             CombinerState::UpdatedVersion{ queued_ops, tail } => {
669:                 // the global tail may have already advanced...
670:                 // tail <= self.tail // by transitivity: self.version_upper_bound <= self.tail
671:                 // update the ctail value
672:                 &&& tail <= self.version_upper_bound
673:                 // the local tail should be smaller than this one here
674:                 &&& self.local_versions[node_id] <= tail
675:                 // the log now contains all entries up to tail
676:                 &&& LogContainsEntriesUpToHere(self.log, tail)
677:                 &&& LogRangeNoNodeId(self.log, tail, self.tail, node_id)
678:                 &&& QueueRidsUpdateDone(queued_ops, self.local_updates, queued_ops.len())
679:                 &&& seq_unique(queued_ops)
680:             }
681:         }
682:     }

685:     /// the log contains entries up to the global tail
686:     /// Inv_LogEntriesGlobalTail(s)
687:     ///
688:     /// Inv_LogEntriesUpToCTailExists(s) && Inv_LogEntriesUpToLocalTailExist(s) are implied
689:     #[invariant]
690:     pub fn inv_log_complete(&self) -> bool {
691:         &&& LogContainsEntriesUpToHere(self.log, self.tail)
692:         &&& LogNoEntriesFromHere(self.log, self.tail)
693:     }

696:     /// Wellformed local update state
697:     /// Inv_LocalUpdatesIdx(s)
698:     #[invariant]
699:     pub fn inv_local_updates(&self) -> bool {
700:         forall |rid| (#[trigger] self.local_updates.contains_key(rid))
701:             ==>  self.inv_local_updates_wf(self.local_updates[rid])
702:     }
703: 
704:     pub open spec fn inv_local_updates_wf(&self, update: UpdateState<DT>) -> bool {
705:         match update {
706:             UpdateState::Init { op } => { true },
707:             UpdateState::Placed { op: _, idx } => {
708:                 &&& self.log.contains_key(idx)
709:                 &&& idx < self.tail
710:             },
711:             UpdateState::Applied { ret, idx } => {
712:                 &&& self.log.contains_key(idx)
713:                 &&& idx < self.tail
714:             },
715:             UpdateState::Done { ret, idx } => {
716:                 &&& self.log.contains_key(idx)
717:                 &&& idx < self.version_upper_bound
718:             },
719:         }
720:     }

723:     /// The results of the read operation must match
724:     /// Inv_ReadOnlyResult(s)
725:     #[invariant]
726:     pub fn inv_read_results(&self) -> bool {
727:         forall |rid| (#[trigger] self.local_reads.contains_key(rid))
728:              ==>  self.read_results_match(self.local_reads[rid])
729:     }
730: 
731:     pub open spec fn read_results_match(&self, read: ReadonlyState<DT>) -> bool {
732:         match read {
733:             ReadonlyState::Done { ret, version_upper_bound, op, .. } => {
734:                 exists |v: nat| (#[trigger] rangeincl(version_upper_bound, v, self.version_upper_bound))
735:                     && ret == DT::dispatch_spec(compute_nrstate_at_version(self.log, v), op)
736:             },
737:             _ => true,
738:         }
739:     }
740: 
741: 
742:     /// The results of the updates must match
743:     /// Inv_UpdateResults(s)
744:     #[invariant]
745:     pub fn inv_update_results(&self) -> bool {
746:         forall |rid| (#[trigger] self.local_updates.contains_key(rid))
747:             ==>  self.update_results_match(self.local_updates[rid])
748:     }
749: 
750:     pub open spec fn update_results_match(&self, update: UpdateState<DT>) -> bool {
751:         match update {
752:             UpdateState::Applied { ret, idx } => {
753:                 ret == DT::dispatch_mut_spec(compute_nrstate_at_version(self.log, idx), self.log[idx].op).1
754:             },
755:             UpdateState::Done { ret, idx } => {
756:                 ret == DT::dispatch_mut_spec(compute_nrstate_at_version(self.log, idx), self.log[idx].op).1
757:             },
758:             _ => true,
759:         }
760:     }

763:     /// All combiners must have distinct request ids they are working on
764:     /// Inv_CombinerRidsDistinct(s)
765:     #[invariant]
766:     pub fn inv_combiner_rids_distinct(&self) -> bool
767:     {
768:       forall |node_id1, node_id2|
769:           (#[trigger] self.combiner.contains_key(node_id1)
770:           && #[trigger] self.combiner.contains_key(node_id2)
771:           && node_id1 != node_id2) ==>
772:             seq_disjoint(self.combiner[node_id1].queued_ops(), self.combiner[node_id2].queued_ops())
773:     }

776:     /// the state of the replica must match the current version of the log
777:     #[invariant]
778:     pub open spec fn replica_state(&self) -> bool {
779:         forall |node_id| (#[trigger] self.replicas.contains_key(node_id)) ==>
780:             self.replicas[node_id] == compute_nrstate_at_version(self.log, self.current_local_version(node_id))
781:     }

784:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
785:     // State Machine Initialization
786:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
787: 
788:     init!{
789:         initialize(number_of_nodes: nat) {
790:             require(number_of_nodes > 0);
791: 
792:             init num_replicas = number_of_nodes;
793:             init log = Map::empty();
794:             init tail = 0;
795:             init replicas = Map::new(Set::range(0, number_of_nodes), |n| DT::init_spec());
796:             init local_versions = Map::new(Set::range(0, number_of_nodes), |n| 0);
797:             init version_upper_bound = 0;
798:             init local_reads = Map::empty();
799:             init local_updates = Map::empty();
800:             init combiner = Map::new(Set::range(0, number_of_nodes), |n| CombinerState::Ready);
801:         }
802:     }
803: 
804:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
805:     // Readonly Transitions
806:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
807: 
808:     /// Read Request: Read the version of the log
809:     ///
810:     /// The algorithm waits while local_version < read_version
811:     transition!{
812:         readonly_version_upper_bound(rid: ReqId) {
813:             remove local_reads -= [ rid => let ReadonlyState::Init { op } ];
814:             add    local_reads += [ rid => ReadonlyState::VersionUpperBound {
815:                                                 op, version_upper_bound: pre.version_upper_bound } ];
816:         }
817:     }
818: 
819:     /// Read Request: wait until the version of the state has reached the version of the log
820:     ///
821:     /// The algorithm waits while local_version < read_version
822:     transition!{
823:         readonly_ready_to_read(rid: ReqId, node_id: NodeId) {
824:             remove local_reads    -= [ rid => let ReadonlyState::VersionUpperBound { op, version_upper_bound } ];
825:             have   local_versions >= [ node_id => let local_head ];
826: 
827:             require(local_head >= version_upper_bound);
828: 
829:             add local_reads += [ rid => ReadonlyState::ReadyToRead{op, node_id, version_upper_bound} ];
830:         }
831:     }
832: 
833:     /// Read Request: perform the read request on the local replica, the combiner must not be busy
834:     transition!{
835:         readonly_apply(rid: ReqId) {
836:             remove local_reads -= [ rid => let ReadonlyState::ReadyToRead { op, node_id, version_upper_bound } ];
837:             have   combiner    >= [ node_id => CombinerState::Ready ];
838:             have   replicas    >= [ node_id => let state ];
839: 
840:             let ret = DT::dispatch_spec(state, op);
841: 
842:             add local_reads += [ rid => ReadonlyState::Done{ op, node_id, version_upper_bound, ret } ];
843:         }
844:     }
845: 
846:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
847:     // Update Transitions
848:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
849: 
850:     /// Combiner: Collect the operations and place them into the log
851:     transition!{
852:         update_place_ops_in_log_one(node_id: NodeId, rid: ReqId) {
853:             // Only allowing a single request at a time
854:             // (in contrast to the seagull one which does it in bulk).
855:             // Hopefully this leads to some easier proofs.
856:             remove combiner      -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Placed{ queued_ops } ];
857:             remove local_updates -= [ rid => let UpdateState::Init{ op }];
858: 
859:             update tail = pre.tail + 1;
860:             add log           += [ pre.tail => LogEntry{ op, node_id }];
861:             add local_updates += [ rid => UpdateState::Placed{ op, idx: pre.tail }];
862:             add combiner      += [ node_id => CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops: queued_ops.push(rid) } ];
863:         }
864:     }
865: 
866:     transition!{
867:         update_done(rid:ReqId) {
868:             remove local_updates -= [ rid => let UpdateState::Applied { ret, idx } ];
869: 
870:             // we must have applied the
871:             require(pre.version_upper_bound > idx);
872: 
873:             add local_updates += [ rid => UpdateState::Done { ret, idx } ];
874:         }
875:     }
876: 
877:     /*/// Update: Remove a finished update from the system
878:     transition!{
879:         update_finish(rid:ReqId) {
880:             remove local_updates -= [ rid => let UpdateState::Done { ret, idx } ];
881:         }
882:     }*/
883: 
884: 
885:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
886:     // Combiner Execute Transitions
887:     ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
888: 
889: 
890:     /// Combiner: start the combiner to execute the update operations on the local replica
891:     transition!{
892:         exec_trivial_start(node_id: NodeId) {
893:             remove combiner -= [ node_id => CombinerState::Ready ];
894: 
895:             add    combiner += [ node_id => CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops: Seq::empty() } ];
896:         }
897:     }
898: 
899:     /// Combiner: read the version of the local replica
900:     transition!{
901:         exec_load_local_version(node_id: NodeId) {
902:             remove combiner      -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops } ];
903: 
904:             have   local_versions >= [node_id => let lversion];
905: 
906:             add    combiner      += [ node_id => CombinerState::LoadedLocalVersion { queued_ops, lversion }];
907:         }
908:     }
909: 
910:     /// Combiner: read the global tail
911:     transition!{
912:         exec_load_global_head(node_id: NodeId) {
913:             remove combiner -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::LoadedLocalVersion { queued_ops, lversion } ];
914: 
915:             add    combiner += [ node_id => CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, lversion, idx: 0, tail: pre.tail } ];
916:         }
917:     }
918: 
919:     /// Combiner: Safety condition, the queue index must be within bounds
920:     property!{
921:         pre_exec_dispatch_local(node_id: NodeId) {
922:             have combiner >= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Loop{ queued_ops, lversion, tail, idx } ];
923:             have log      >= [ lversion => let log_entry ];
924: 
925:             require(log_entry.node_id == node_id);
926:             require(lversion < tail);
927:             assert(idx < queued_ops.len()) by {
928:                 // assert(pre.wf_combiner_for_node_id(node_id));
929:                 // assert(lversion < tail);
930:                 // assert(pre.log.index(lversion).node_id == node_id);
931:             };
932:             assert(queued_ops.len() > 0);
933:         }
934:     }
935: 
936:     /// Combiner: dispatch a local update and apply it to the local replica and record the outcome of the update
937:     transition!{
938:         exec_dispatch_local(node_id: NodeId) {
939:             remove combiner      -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, lversion, tail, idx } ];
940:             remove replicas      -= [ node_id => let old_nr_state ];
941:             let rid = queued_ops.index(idx as int);
942:             remove local_updates -= [ rid => let local_update ];
943: 
944:             have log >= [lversion => let log_entry];
945: 
946:             // require(local_update.is_Placed());
947: 
948:             // apply all updates between lhead and global tail that were enqueued from local node
949:             require(lversion < tail);
950:             require(log_entry.node_id == node_id);
951:             let (new_nr_state, ret) = DT::dispatch_mut_spec(old_nr_state, log_entry.op);
952: 
953:             add local_updates += [ rid => UpdateState::Applied { ret, idx: lversion }];
954:             add replicas      += [ node_id => new_nr_state];
955:             add combiner      += [ node_id => CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, lversion: lversion + 1, tail, idx: idx + 1}];
956:         }
957:     }
958: 
959:     /// Combiner: dispatch a remote update and apply it to the local replica
960:     transition!{
961:         exec_dispatch_remote(node_id: NodeId) {
962:             remove combiner -= [ node_id => let CombinerState:: Loop { queued_ops, lversion, tail, idx } ];
963:             remove replicas -= [ node_id => let old_nr_state ];
964: 
965:             have   log      >= [ lversion => let log_entry ];
966: 
967:             // apply all updates between lhead and global tail that were enqueued from remote nodes
968:             require(lversion < tail);
969:             require(log_entry.node_id != node_id);
970:             let (new_nr_state, ret) = DT::dispatch_mut_spec(old_nr_state, log_entry.op);
971: 
972:             add replicas    += [ node_id => new_nr_state ];
973:             add combiner    += [ node_id => CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, lversion: lversion + 1, tail, idx}];
974:         }
975:     }
976: 
977:     /// Combiner: Safety condition, if we applied all updates, idx must be the length of the list
978:     property!{
979:         pre_exec_update_version_upper_bound(node_id: NodeId) {
980:             have combiner >= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Loop{ queued_ops, lversion, tail, idx } ];
981: 
982:             require(lversion == tail);
983:             assert(idx == queued_ops.len()) by {
984:                 // assert(pre.wf_combiner_for_node_id(node_id));
985:                 // assert(lversion == tail);
986:             };
987:         }
988:     }
989: 
990:     /// Combiner: update the version upper bound when all updates have been applied to the local replica
991:     transition!{
992:         exec_update_version_upper_bound(node_id: NodeId) {
993:             remove combiner -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::Loop { queued_ops, lversion, tail, idx, }];
994: 
995:             // we applied all updates up to the global tail we've read
996:             require(lversion == tail);
997: 
998:             // assert(idx == queued_ops.len()) by {
999:             //     //assert(pre.wf_combiner_for_node_id(node_id));
1000:             // };
1001: 
1002:             update version_upper_bound = if pre.version_upper_bound >= tail {
1003:                 pre.version_upper_bound
1004:             } else {
1005:                 tail
1006:             };
1007:             add combiner += [ node_id => CombinerState::UpdatedVersion { queued_ops, tail } ];
1008:         }
1009:     }
1010: 
1011:     /// Combiner: is done, bump the local version and combiner returns to ready state
1012:     transition!{
1013:         exec_finish(node_id: NodeId) {
1014:             remove combiner       -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::UpdatedVersion { queued_ops, tail } ];
1015:             remove local_versions -= [ node_id => let old_local_head ];
1016: 
1017:             // here have the local updates updated to done.
1018: 
1019:             add    local_versions += [ node_id => tail ];
1020:             add    combiner       += [ node_id => CombinerState::Ready ];
1021:         }
1022:     }
1023: 
1024:     /// Combiner: is done, without any change
1025:     transition!{
1026:         exec_finish_no_change(node_id: NodeId) {
1027:             remove combiner -= [ node_id => let CombinerState::LoadedLocalVersion { queued_ops, lversion } ];
1028: 
1029:             require(lversion == pre.tail);
1030:             assert(queued_ops.len() == 0);
1031: 
1032:             add    combiner += [ node_id => CombinerState::Ready];
1033:         }
1034:     }

1042:     #[inductive(initialize)]
1043:     fn initialize_inductive(post: Self, number_of_nodes: nat) {
1044: 
1045:         // XXX: is it really that hard to show finetness of map domain?
1046:         let max_dom = (post.num_replicas - 1) as nat;
1047:         let cmap = map_new_rec(max_dom, CombinerState::Ready);
1048:         assert(cmap.dom().finite()) by {
1049:             map_new_rec_dom_finite(max_dom, CombinerState::Ready);
1050:         }
1051:         assert(forall |n: nat| 0 <= n < post.num_replicas <==> post.combiner.contains_key(n));
1052:         assert(forall |n: nat| 0 <= n <= max_dom <==> cmap.contains_key(n)) by {
1053:             map_new_rec_dom_finite(max_dom, CombinerState::Ready);
1054:         }
1055:         assert(forall |n: nat| 0 <= n <= max_dom <==> cmap.contains_key(n));
1056:         assert(forall |n: nat| 0 <= n < post.num_replicas <==> cmap.contains_key(n));
1057: 
1058:         assert(forall |n: nat| post.combiner.contains_key(n) <==> #[trigger]cmap.contains_key(n));
1059:         assert(post.combiner.dom() =~= cmap.dom());
1060:         assert(forall |n| #[trigger]post.combiner.contains_key(n) ==> post.combiner[n] == CombinerState::Ready);
1061: 
1062:         assert(forall |n| #[trigger]cmap.contains_key(n) ==> cmap[n] == CombinerState::Ready) by {
1063:             map_new_rec_dom_finite(max_dom, CombinerState::Ready);
1064:         }
1065:         assert(post.combiner =~= cmap);
1066:         // assert_maps_equal!(post.combiner, cmap);
1067:     }

1079:     pub proof fn add_ticket_inductive(
1080:         pre: UnboundedLog::State<DT>,
1081:         post: UnboundedLog::State<DT>,
1082:         input: InputOperation<DT>,
1083:         rid: ReqId,
1084:     )
1085:         requires pre.invariant(),
1086:             add_ticket(pre, post, input, rid),
1087:             rid == get_fresh_nat(pre.local_updates.dom() + pre.local_reads.dom(), pre.combiner)
1088:         ensures post.invariant(),
1089:     {
1090:         get_fresh_nat_not_in(pre.local_updates.dom() + pre.local_reads.dom(), pre.combiner);
1091:         match input {
1092:             InputOperation::Read(op) => {
1093:                 assert(post.inv_readonly_requests_wf());
1094:             }
1095:             InputOperation::Write(op) => {
1096:                 assert forall |node_id| #[trigger] post.combiner.contains_key(node_id) implies post.wf_combiner_for_node_id(node_id) by {
1097:                     assert(post.combiner[node_id] == pre.combiner[node_id]);
1098:                     match post.combiner[node_id] {
1099:                         CombinerState::Placed { queued_ops } => {
1100:                             LogRangeMatchesQueue_update_change(queued_ops, post.log, 0, post.local_versions[node_id], post.tail, node_id, pre.local_updates, post.local_updates);
